exposure: Cancer diagnosis in adolescence or young adulthood (AYA)
cohort: Adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer survivors (diagnosed at ages 15-39 years) and a comparison cohort of women without a cancer diagnosis
finding: AYA cancer survivors had a higher prevalence of preterm birth, low birth weight, and cesarean delivery compared to women without a cancer diagnosis, particularly among those diagnosed during pregnancy and those treated with chemotherapy.
mod_finding: The prevalence of cesarean delivery was significantly higher among AYA cancer survivors compared to the comparison cohort (PR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.01-1.14).
